title: Managing a stage boundary: purpose, objectives and context
blurb: Explain what managing a stage boundary gives the project board, when it runs, and how it is also used to prepare exception plans.
question: A stage is nearly finished. The board wants to know how it went, what the next stage involves and whether the project is still worth doing. Which process provides this, and when is it used?

teach.h: Getting the board ready to decide
teach.body: Formally: managing a stage boundary enables the project manager to give the project board enough information to review how successful the current stage has been, look at the plan for the next stage, review the updated project plan, and confirm that the business justification and the risks are still acceptable. In plain English: before the board commits to another stage, the PM packages up everything it needs to make that call. It runs at, or close to, the end of each stage.

teach.h: Objectives at a normal stage end
items: Assure the board that all products in the current stage plan are completed and approved.
Prepare the stage plan for the next stage.
Review and, if needed, update the PID: business case, project plan, user's quality expectations, management approaches, team structure and role descriptions.
Give the board the information it needs to judge whether the project is still viable.
Record lessons that can help later stages or other projects.
Request authorization to start the next stage.

items.label: First use: plan the first delivery stage
To prepare an exception plan, even in the final stage
Not used: closing a project runs instead

teach.h: Two reasons to enter the process

teach.caption: For exceptions, the objectives are similar but include preparing an exception plan and seeking approval to replace the current plan with it.

teach.h: Its place in the exception technique
teach.caption: Managing a stage boundary is the means by which the exception procedure is carried out.

teach.body: Thornbury District Council is digitizing its local archive in four stages. Near the end of stage 2, project manager Abena Mensah confirms all stage 2 products are approved, prepares the stage 3 plan, updates the project plan and business case, and writes the end stage report. Executive Rhys Morgan's board reviews it all. Because a new government grant has changed the funding picture, the board checks the business case is still sound before it authorizes stage 3.

The process rests on dividing the project into stages. At each boundary the board may decide to stop the project. If the business justification has gone, closing the project is a sensible decision, not a failure: it stops money being spent on something no longer worth doing.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Managing a stage boundary is NOT run at the end of the final stage; closing a project is part of the final stage. (2) Reporting highlights at regular intervals is controlling a stage, not this process. (3) Exception plans are prepared HERE, not in controlling a stage, and can be prepared in any stage, including the final one.

items: Purpose: give the board what it needs to review the stage, look at the next stage plan and the updated project plan, and confirm justification and risks.
Runs at or near the end of every stage except the final stage; first used at the end of initiation.
Also used at any time to prepare an exception plan requested by the board.
Reviews and updates the PID, records lessons and requests the next stage.
The board may stop the project at a boundary; that is not a failure.

summary: You can now explain the purpose and objectives of managing a stage boundary, when it runs and how it carries out the exception procedure. You can also separate it from controlling a stage and closing a project.

A.q: Which is a purpose of the managing a stage boundary process?
options: Control the link between the PM and the team managers
Assign work and monitor it during the stage
Confirm the acceptance of the project's main product
Let the board confirm continued business justification
A.why: Managing a stage boundary gives the board enough information to review the stage and confirm continued business justification and acceptable risks (manual 18.1).

whyNot.0: Controlling the PM to team manager link is managing product delivery.
whyNot.1: Assigning and monitoring work is controlling a stage.
whyNot.2: Confirming acceptance of the project product is closing a project.

A.q: When is the managing a stage boundary process normally carried out?
options: At or close to the end of each stage
At the start of each new delivery stage
Once, at the end of the initiation stage
At each agreed highlight reporting point
A.why: The process is executed at, or close to, the end of each stage (except the final stage) (manual 18.1).

whyNot.1: By the time the new stage starts, the board must already have authorized it on the basis of this process.
whyNot.2: It is first used at the end of initiation but is repeated at the end of each later stage.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports at agreed intervals belong to controlling a stage.

A.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
Managing a stage boundary provides the means by which the [?] procedure can be carried out.
options: closure
quality
exception
initiation
A.why: Managing a stage boundary is the means of implementing the exception procedure: exception plans are prepared here (manual 18.3).

whyNot.0: Closure procedures belong to closing a project.
whyNot.1: Quality procedures are set out in the quality management approach.
whyNot.3: Initiation is carried out in initiating a project.

B.q:
Which two statements about when managing a stage boundary is used are correct?
1. It is first used at the end of the initiation stage.
2. It is used at the end of the final stage to hand over the products.
3. It can be used to prepare an exception plan during the final stage.
4. It is used to send highlight reports at agreed intervals.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: It is first used at the end of initiation (1) and can prepare exception plans at any time, including in the final stage (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: closing a project, not a stage boundary, ends the final stage.
whyNot.2: Both are false: handover is in closing a project, and highlight reports are in controlling a stage.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: highlight reports belong to controlling a stage.

B.q: At a stage boundary the board decides to stop the project because the business case is no longer viable. How should this decision be viewed?
options: As a failure of the project manager
As a breach that needs an exception plan
As a valid outcome of the boundary review
As a reason to skip closing the project
B.why: A stage boundary is a decision point; stopping a project whose justification has gone is a sound decision, not a failure (manual 18.3).

whyNot.0: Stopping an unjustified project reflects good control, not PM failure.
whyNot.1: An exception plan replaces a plan forecast to exceed tolerance; it is not how a stop decision is handled.
whyNot.3: A premature close still needs the closing a project process, tailored to the situation.

B.q: Which objective of managing a stage boundary applies to exceptions?
options: Seek approval to replace a plan with an exception plan
Raise an exception report on the forecast tolerance breach
Request authorization to start the next stage
Assure the board that all stage products are approved
B.why: For exceptions, the objectives include preparing an exception plan and seeking approval to replace the project or current stage plan with it (manual 18.2).

whyNot.1: The exception report is raised in controlling a stage (escalate issues and risks) before the board asks for an exception plan; it is not a stage boundary objective.
whyNot.2: Requesting the next stage is the objective at a normal stage end.
whyNot.3: Assuring the board that products are complete is a normal stage end objective.

C.q: Which process runs at the end of the initiation stage, and what does it prepare for the first delivery stage?
options: Initiating a project; a project plan
Managing a stage boundary; a stage plan
Controlling a stage; a work package
Directing a project; a team plan
C.why: Managing a stage boundary is first used at the end of initiation, where the PM prepares the stage plan for the first delivery stage.

whyNot.0: Initiating a project creates the project plan, but the next stage plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.2: Controlling a stage authorizes work packages during a delivery stage.
whyNot.3: Directing a project is the board's process; team plans belong to team managers.

C.q: Who requests an exception plan, and in which process is it prepared?
options: The project manager; controlling a stage
The team manager; managing product delivery
The project board; controlling a stage
The project board; managing a stage boundary
C.why: The board requests an exception plan in response to an exception report, and the PM prepares it in managing a stage boundary.

whyNot.0: The PM raises the exception report; the board requests the plan, and it is not prepared in controlling a stage.
whyNot.1: Team managers escalate work package issues to the PM; they do not request exception plans.
whyNot.2: The board does request it, but it is prepared in managing a stage boundary.

C.q: Which two products does managing a stage boundary update so that the board can judge whether the project is still viable?
options: Project plan and business case
Team plan and checkpoint report
Project brief and project mandate
Highlight report and daily log
C.why: The PM updates the project plan and the business case at a stage boundary; the board reviews them to confirm continued justification (manual 18.1, 18.2).

whyNot.1: Team plans and checkpoint reports belong to team managers in managing product delivery.
whyNot.2: The brief and mandate are pre-project inputs, superseded by the PID.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports and the daily log are used during the stage, not to confirm viability at the boundary.

reteach.title: The pit stop
reteach.question: In a long motor race, what happens at each pit stop before the car goes out again?

blocks.body: The crew checks how the last stint went, plans the next stint (fuel, tyres), updates the race plan and asks whether the car can still win. The team principal then sends the car out, changes strategy or retires it. Managing a stage boundary is the pit stop: the PM prepares, the board decides.

blocks.text: There is no pit stop after the chequered flag: the final stage ends with closing a project, not a stage boundary.

explain.body: Enough information to review the current stage's success, look at the next stage plan, review the updated project plan, and confirm justification and acceptable risks.

test.q: Which is NOT something managing a stage boundary gives the board information to do?
options: Review the success of the current stage
Authorize a work package for a team
Review the updated project plan
Confirm continued business justification
test.why: Work packages are authorized by the PM in controlling a stage; the other three are part of the purpose of managing a stage boundary (manual 18.1).

whyNot.0: Reviewing the current stage's success is part of the purpose.
whyNot.2: Reviewing the updated project plan is part of the purpose.
whyNot.3: Confirming continued business justification is part of the purpose.

explain.body: A boundary runs at the end of initiation and at the end of every delivery stage except the last. A four-stage project has three planned boundaries.

test.q: A project has four management stages, including initiation. At how many planned stage ends is managing a stage boundary used?
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
test.why: It runs at the end of stages 1, 2 and 3 but not at the end of the final stage, so three times.

whyNot.0: Two misses one of the boundaries before the final stage.
whyNot.2: Four wrongly includes the end of the final stage, where closing a project runs instead.
whyNot.3: Five is more than the number of stages.

explain.body: When the board requests one, the PM prepares an exception plan here. Its approval marks a stage boundary for the revised stage, even though it comes before the planned stage end.

test.q: What does the board's approval of an exception plan mark?
options: The premature close of the project
The end of the project's final stage
A return to the initiation stage
A stage boundary for the revised stage
test.why: Although produced before the planned stage end, an approved exception plan marks a stage boundary for the revised stage.

whyNot.0: Premature closure is a separate board decision handled by closing a project.
whyNot.1: Exception plans can be approved in any stage and do not end the final stage.
whyNot.2: Initiation happens once; an exception plan creates a revised delivery stage.

explain.body: At a boundary the board can authorize the next stage, ask for changes, or stop the project if its justification has gone.

test.q: Which decision is open to the project board after reviewing a stage boundary?
options: Hand work packages straight to team managers
Rewrite the project mandate from the business
Stop the project if its justification has gone
Skip the next stage plan to save time
test.why: The board may decide to stop the project at a boundary; this is not a failure if the justification no longer exists (manual 18.3).

whyNot.0: Work packages are authorized by the PM, not handed out by the board.
whyNot.1: The mandate comes from the business layer before the project starts.
whyNot.3: A stage only starts when the board authorizes its plan, so the plan cannot be skipped.
